artifact.status_search_result: Axiomatic approaches to algorithmic information theory have been proposed, notably by M. Burgin (1982, following the style of Blum's axioms for computational complexity), which subsume plain and prefix complexity as instances of axiomatically defined information measures. These give partial axiomatizations, but a universally accepted, complete axiomatic foundation from which the full body of AIT is uniformly derived is not established; the question is therefore best regarded as partially solved / still open in its strong form.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic information theory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: An axiomatic approach to algorithmic information theory based on the Blum axioms (Blum 1967) was introduced by Mark Burgin in a paper presented for publication by Andrey Kolmogorov (Burgin 1982).
status_evidence.claim: A partial axiomatization in the Blum-axiom style exists (Burgin 1982), encompassing several AIT measures as special cases.

status_evidence.snippet: Problems collected from G. J. Chaitin, F. Geurts, H. Jürgensen, T. Odor and K. Svozil.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in a list of open problems in AIT attributed to several authors including Jürgensen.
